documents.title: Architecture Decisions from Track A Audit

concepts.label: Configurable DD/IC Pipeline Stages
concepts.summary: Each fund can define its own DD/IC pipeline stages and sequence; ships with a sensible default.

concepts.label: DealResearchDoc Unified Document System
concepts.summary: DealResearchDoc becomes the single document system; adds 'quick-note' type alongside 'memo', 'competitor', 'market'; memos.ts deleted.

concepts.label: Light List + Full Detail Call Pattern
concepts.summary: List views return summary fields (title, date, participants); detail views return full data (transcript, metrics, risks, tasks).

concepts.label: Configurable Scoring Dimensions per Fund Thesis
concepts.summary: Ships with 6-8 default scoring dimensions; each fund can configure weights and add/remove dimensions during thesis setup.

concepts.label: deal_contacts Join Table
concepts.summary: Relationship table with role, isPrimary, addedAt fields; reuses existing DealContactAssociation type.

concepts.label: Security Quick-Wins Deferred to Phase 2
concepts.summary: Security issues are documented only; full fixes deferred until Phase 2 after audit completion.

concepts.label: Configurable Deal Metrics Schema per Fund
concepts.summary: Deal.metrics schema is configurable per fund; needs separate design session for frontend/backend implementation.

concepts.label: Soft Stage Enforcement with Partner Override
concepts.summary: Warn when skipping stages; partners can override. No hard blocking.

concepts.label: Structured PassDecision Entity
concepts.summary: Pass/decline tracking with reason category, free-text notes, stage-at-pass, reviewer; enables learning loop.

concepts.label: DDChecklist First-Class Entity
concepts.summary: DDChecklist type with areas, items, status, assignee, notes, linked reference calls.

concepts.label: Single Comprehensive ThesisConfig
concepts.summary: Two ThesisConfig types merged into one with both structured fields and free-text overview.

concepts.label: FSD shared→widget Inversion Fix (Phase 2)
concepts.summary: ChatMessage types to be extracted to shared/types/ai-chat.ts before backend build; deferred to Phase 2.

concepts.label: Stage-Aware Fixture Factories
concepts.summary: Pre-Seed caps at $20K MRR/$10M val; Seed at $100K/$25M; Series A at $500K/$100M — fixtures reflect realistic stage-correlated metrics.

concepts.label: Co-Investor Tracking on Deal
concepts.summary: coInvestors array added to Deal type: name, firm, isLead, status (confirmed/verbal/interested/passed).

concepts.label: Deal Ownership and Term Sheet Fields Deferred to V2
concepts.summary: V1 focuses on screening/evaluation; term sheet and ownership fields deferred to V2.

concepts.label: Passive Email Capture + Email Tab
concepts.summary: Both active email tab and passive capture are included in scope.

relationships.detail: Both follow the same per-fund configurability pattern established for the DD pipeline.
Round types, metrics, and stages are all consistently configurable per fund thesis.
DDChecklist links reference calls, which are part of the unified DealResearchDoc document system.
PassDecision captures the stage-at-pass field, complementing soft stage enforcement with an audit trail.
ThesisConfig holds the scoring dimension weights and fund-specific configuration.
Both are architectural clean-up items explicitly deferred from Phase 1 to Phase 2.
co-investor tracking extends the same relationship-table pattern established for deal-contact associations.

concepts.label: Maverick-as-Employee Framing
concepts.summary: Maverick is positioned as a single AI VC Associate hired to do a job, not 7 sub-agents sharing a frontend; sub-agents are internal implementation details.

concepts.label: VC Core Workflow: SIGNAL→SCREEN→RESEARCH→BRIEF→MEMO
concepts.summary: The five-stage workflow Maverick must own end-to-end as a hired associate.

concepts.label: Maverick Positioning: True AI Teammate
concepts.summary: 'Not a tool. Not a feature. A true AI teammate.' — VCs want fewer tools, ideally one that does the work, not just displays it.

concepts.label: VC Associate Workload Model
concepts.summary: 300-800 first-pass looks/year, 5-10 detailed DD processes, 3-6 memos; time split: 40% info gathering, 20% modeling, 20% writing, 15% meetings, 5% CRM.

concepts.label: Maverick Internal Sub-Agents
concepts.summary: Deck Parser, Fit Scorer, Call Summarizer, Memo Drafter, Email Drafter, Research Agent, Ask-the-Analyst — internal neural circuits, not user-facing products.

concepts.label: Contact Management as Essential Capability
concepts.summary: 60-70% of deals come from warm intros; contact management was promoted to ESSENTIAL in the 2026-04-07 validation session.

concepts.label: Proactive Notification Center
concepts.summary: Maverick must alert partners proactively about stale deals, upcoming meetings, new high-fit deals; priority elevated in validation.

concepts.label: Voice Notes Capability
concepts.summary: New essential capability added in 2026-04-07 validation; enables quick capture during calls and fieldwork.

concepts.label: Multi-Fund Architecture
concepts.summary: Organization → Fund → Team hierarchy; new essential capability identified in 2026-04-07 validation.

concepts.label: Multi-Channel Agent Output
concepts.summary: Maverick must operate across multiple channels (email, Slack, in-app); capability elevated in validation.

concepts.label: Conversational Workflow Execution
concepts.summary: New essential capability: Maverick runs workflows conversationally, not just through structured UI.

concepts.label: Custom Fields as Essential Capability
concepts.summary: Custom fields via JSONB on all entities; identified as essential in 2026-04-07 validation.

concepts.label: Day-One Associate Bootstrap Capabilities
concepts.summary: Know the team, manage relationships, set up integrations, handle notifications, prepare for meetings, run workflows autonomously.

relationships.detail: The employee framing means sub-agents are internal implementation details; they must not be exposed as separate products.
'True AI teammate' positioning is the market-facing expression of the employee framing.
Each stage of SIGNAL→SCREEN→RESEARCH→BRIEF→MEMO maps to one or more internal sub-agents.
The workload model (300-800 decks, 5-10 DD, 40% info gathering) defines the volume and time distribution that the core workflow must handle.
60-70% warm intro stat from the workload model directly motivates contact management being essential.
Each fund in the hierarchy needs its own custom field configurations via JSONB.
Conversational workflow execution is one expression of multi-channel agent output.
Proactive notifications are explicitly listed as a Day-One capability: alert about stale deals, meetings, high-fit deals.

concepts.label: Feature-Sliced Design (FSD) Layer Structure
concepts.summary: app/widgets/features/entities/shared hierarchy with 14 widgets, 40 features, 9 entities — structure is sound.

concepts.label: FSD Critical Inversion: shared imports from widgets
concepts.summary: shared/ imports from widgets/ai-chat in 6+ production files (providers, hooks, lib, molecules), creating a circular dependency that violates FSD's core principle.

concepts.label: ESLint Boundary Coverage Gap (~25%)
concepts.summary: Only 9/14 widgets, 3/40 features, 2/9 entities have boundary rules; the rest fall through to permissive layer-level fallbacks.

concepts.label: React Context-Only State (No Zustand)
concepts.summary: All state in 4 React Context providers and local useState — clean today but will not scale to cross-widget coordination.

concepts.label: DealResearchRepo Not Wired into ServicesProvider
concepts.summary: DealResearchRepo is defined but not in Services type or provider context, creating a gap where deal-research features cannot access the repository through DI.

concepts.label: Fixture Data Shipped to Production Bundle
concepts.summary: DealWorkspace imports DealWorkspace.fixture.ts mock data in production code, shipping test data to production bundles.

concepts.label: God Component Files
concepts.summary: 8 files exceed 500 LOC; message-router.tsx at 2,404 lines is largest, with ThenSection.tsx (1,233) and AIChatPanel.tsx (1,247) also critical candidates for decomposition.

concepts.label: message-router.tsx Decomposition
concepts.summary: 2,404-line file handles keyword routing for all chat message types and inlines 66+ mock data references; must be split into route registry + per-route handlers.

concepts.label: ThenSection.tsx Decomposition
concepts.summary: 1,233-line file handles ALL workflow action types; must extract each action config (NotifyTeamConfig, SendEmailConfig, etc.) using a registry pattern.

concepts.label: AIChatPanel.tsx Decomposition
concepts.summary: 1,247-line chat panel; must extract useChatMessages hook, ChatHeader, ThreadHistoryPanel, ChatScrollManager.

concepts.label: Organization → Fund → Team Multi-Fund Hierarchy
concepts.summary: Architectural decision from 2026-04-07 validation: multi-fund hierarchy uses Organization → Fund → Team structure.

concepts.label: AgentResponse Must Be Channel-Agnostic
concepts.summary: AgentResponse interface must not be tied to a specific output channel; required for multi-channel operation.

concepts.label: Custom Fields via JSONB on All Entities
concepts.summary: Custom fields implemented via JSONB column on all entities, not a separate table per entity.

relationships.detail: The shared→widgets circular import violates FSD's core downward-only dependency principle.
The inversion (shared imports from widgets/ai-chat) is exactly what the Phase 2 fix targets.
Without boundary rules on 75% of modules, FSD layer violations can silently proliferate.
React Context state cannot coordinate across widgets cleanly within FSD boundaries; Zustand or equivalent needed.
The DealResearchDoc decision requires DealResearchRepo to be wired into ServicesProvider to be accessible.
message-router.tsx is the largest god component and the primary candidate for splitting.
ThenSection.tsx handles all workflow action types in a single file — classic god component pattern.
AIChatPanel.tsx combines message handling, file drops, conversation history, thread management, scroll into one file.
The concrete Organization → Fund → Team schema implements the multi-fund architecture capability.
A channel-agnostic AgentResponse is the technical prerequisite for multi-channel output.
JSONB on all entities is the implementation strategy for the custom fields essential capability.

concepts.label: ServicesProvider Dependency Injection Pattern
concepts.summary: Services are injected via a provider context; 5 of 8 service interfaces are currently wired in.

concepts.label: UserSettingsRepo Write-Only Gap
concepts.summary: Six save* methods, zero get* methods; frontend settings pages hardcode initial values, no way to load persisted settings.

concepts.label: DealRepo Missing Mutation Operations
concepts.summary: No create, update, or delete on DealRepo; only updateStage exists; search takes bare string not filter objects.

concepts.label: CallRepo Read-Only and Under-Specified
concepts.summary: Only listForDeal and get; no create/update/delete, no list-all, no filter-by-date, no transcript upload; mock ignores dealId parameter.

concepts.label: MemoRepo 1:1 Deal-to-Memo Assumption
concepts.summary: get(dealId) returns single Memo | null; real workflows produce multiple memos per deal (draft, IC, follow-up); no list, no delete, no versioning.

concepts.label: AgentRunner.run() No Error Path or Lifecycle Hooks
concepts.summary: Returns only { cancel }; no onError, no onComplete, no reconnect logic, no token/cost tracking, no run ID for audit — unusable for production.

concepts.label: AgentResponse — Channel-Agnostic Agent Output Interface
concepts.summary: V2 P0 interface: channel-agnostic agent output; Sprint 0 target; source: GAP-MULTI-CHANNEL.md.

concepts.label: WorkflowIntent — NLP Intent to Structured Workflow Schema
concepts.summary: V2 P0 interface: maps NLP intent to structured workflow schema; Sprint 3-4 target; source: GAP-AI-AUTONOMY.md.

concepts.label: OrganizationRepo + FundRepo — Org/Fund Hierarchy Services
concepts.summary: V2 P0 interfaces for org/fund hierarchy; Sprint 0 target; source: GAP-ORG-CUSTOM.md.

concepts.label: TemplateRegistryService — Fund-Type Template Storage
concepts.summary: V2 P0 interface: fund-type template storage and application; Sprint 0 target; source: GAP-ONBOARDING.md.

concepts.label: ContactRepo Informal Mock Interface
concepts.summary: ContactRepo exists only as a mock interface in fixtures — never promoted to a formal service contract.

concepts.label: V2 P0 Gap Inventory (20 Items)
concepts.summary: Complete P0 gap inventory of 20 items documented in V2-SCOPE-EXPANSION.md Section 2; source for Sprint 0-4 new interfaces.

relationships.detail: DealResearchRepo's absence from ServicesProvider means it bypasses the DI pattern entirely.
A write-only settings repo means backend engineers cannot implement a valid read/write contract.
Missing create/update/delete on DealRepo means the backend cannot implement full CRUD through the DI pattern.
The merged document system requires multiple memos per deal; MemoRepo's 1:1 assumption must be replaced with list+versioning.
A production-grade AgentRunner requires a proper AgentResponse interface with lifecycle hooks and error paths.
The AgentResponse V2 P0 interface is the concrete implementation of the channel-agnostic requirement.
OrganizationRepo and FundRepo are the service-layer implementations of the Organization→Fund→Team hierarchy.
WorkflowIntent maps NLP to structured schemas, which is the backend contract for conversational workflow execution.
Contact management was promoted to ESSENTIAL, but ContactRepo is still an informal mock — this gap must be closed.
AgentResponse is one of the 20 P0 gaps in the V2 scope expansion.
OrganizationRepo+FundRepo are in the V2 P0 gap inventory targeting Sprint 0.
Fund-type templates are stored and applied through TemplateRegistryService, backed by the merged ThesisConfig.

concepts.label: SafeMarkdown with rehype-sanitize
concepts.summary: Well-implemented sanitization component; dangerouslySetInnerHTML completely absent; no hardcoded API keys in codebase.

concepts.label: PDF Export innerHTML DOM Injection Surface
concepts.summary: export-to-pdf.ts uses container.innerHTML = html with escapeHTML(); if any TipTap content bypasses escaping, this creates a DOM injection surface.

concepts.label: Client-Side-Only File Upload Validation
concepts.summary: All MIME type checks are client-side only and trivially bypassable; backend validation absent.

concepts.label: Permissions as UI Decoration Only
concepts.summary: No middleware, no route guards, no server-side enforcement; permissions exist only in the UI layer.

concepts.label: Conversation History in Plaintext localStorage
concepts.summary: Deal data in conversation history stored in plaintext localStorage — no encryption at rest on client.

concepts.label: TipTap Link Extension javascript: URI Vulnerability
concepts.summary: Both TipTap editor instances configure Link extension without protocol restrictions; javascript: URIs stored in documents become executable when exported or shared (CRITICAL severity).

concepts.label: Empty next.config.ts — No CSP or Security Headers
concepts.summary: next.config.ts is completely empty; no Content Security Policy, no security headers configured.

concepts.label: Passive Email/Calendar Capture Security Concern
concepts.summary: New concern from 2026-04-07 validation: passive email and calendar data capture introduces data access and privacy risks.

concepts.label: AI Autonomous Email Sending Security Concern
concepts.summary: New concern from 2026-04-07 validation: AI autonomously sending email requires send-gate controls and audit trail.

concepts.label: Voice Note Privacy Concern
concepts.summary: New concern from 2026-04-07 validation: voice note capture may record ambient or privileged conversations.

concepts.label: Security Risk Level: MEDIUM→HIGH on Backend Connection
concepts.summary: Overall risk is MEDIUM pre-backend, escalating to HIGH once real data flows through these patterns without fixes.

relationships.detail: TipTap documents containing javascript: URIs become executable when exported via the innerHTML PDF export path.
SafeMarkdown correctly sanitizes markdown, but TipTap content follows a different rendering path not covered by SafeMarkdown.
UI-only permissions are one of the key factors driving the risk level to HIGH once a backend is connected.
Client-side-only validation is trivially bypassable and contributes to the elevated risk profile.
Deal data in plaintext localStorage is a confidentiality risk that escalates with real data.
Absence of CSP headers means javascript: URI execution is not blocked at the browser policy level.
AI autonomous email sending was deferred to Phase 2 fixes, but its security implications (send-gate, audit) must be designed before backend build.
The decision to include passive email capture raises the security concerns around data access and privacy that must be addressed in Phase 2.
Voice note capability must be designed with ambient recording privacy constraints in mind.
